title: adaptive-slo-smoothing-via-proactive-throttle-calibration-and-observed-lag-suppression
author: Claire Zhang
release_notes: Introduces an adaptive throttle calibration controller that smooths SLO violations by adjusting tenant-level throttle setpoints with a PID-inspired feedback loop. Improves stability during short regional surges and reduces oscillation between shed and reopen states. Backward compatible; default disabled behind feature flag slo_throttle_cal_v1.
description:
Context and motivation: We continue to see short, noisy spikes in tail latency that cause reactive load-shedding to oscillate (shed → reopen → shed). That behaviour produces high churn for long-running KV-cached sessions and causes tenant-visible error bursts. This PR introduces a controller that observes smoothed SLO deltas and proactively nudges tenant throttle setpoints using a calibrated feedback rule (proportional + integral term) to reduce oscillation and preferentially favor short recovery windows over aggressive immediate shedding.

Goals: reduce oscillatory shedding across regional surges, shorten recovery jitter, keep per-tenant throughput close to target SLO without causing large error spikes, and provide safe rollout controls (feature flag + canary policy).

What this changes: single continuous change set that touches the regional shed executor, the tenant throttler, and the telemetry pipeline: 1) new controller module (slo_throttle_calibrator) implementing a lightweight feedback loop with configurable windowing and rate caps; 2) tenancy API extension for a soft-setpoint (soft_throttle_hint) that the controller can update without overriding operator-set hard limits; 3) metric exports (slo_delta_smoothed, throttle_hint_applied, hint_conflict_count) and traces for decision points; 4) conservative default tuning and a runtime feature flag slo_throttle_cal_v1.

Design notes: the controller operates on a 10s aggregation window by default, computes an exponentially-weighted-smoothed SLO delta, applies a proportional + integral correction (bounded by per-tenant rate of change), and writes a hint to the tenancy config server. The actual enforcement still runs through the existing throttler which treats hints as advisory unless an account-level opt-in flag is set. This minimizes risk while still enabling meaningful smoothing.

Rollout and safety: feature gated behind slo_throttle_cal_v1. Plan: enable in internal canary (5% traffic) for 24h, inspect metrics and traces (tail-latency, hint_conflict_count, shed/reopen frequency); advance to 25% if stable, then 100% across non-enterprise accounts. Enterprise/Dedicated customers default to off unless they opt-in via console toggle. We added an emergency kill-switch that reverts hint application in <1s.

Testing and validation: unit tests for controller math and boundary conditions; integration harness that replays historical surge workloads (simulated tenant skews) to verify reduced shed oscillations; chaos test exercise where a region loses 20% capacity for 3 minutes — we observe 32% fewer reopen events and 18% lower 95th latency volatility in the canary. CI exercises lint, unit, and end-to-end replay job.

Observability: new dashboards (SLO -> Throttle Calibration) and alert: slo_calib_conflict_rate > 0.5% for 15m. Telemetry includes an event stream of hint writes to support postmortems.

Backward compatibility & migration: controller writes only to soft_throttle_hint. Existing operator-set hard_limits remain authoritative. If hint_conflict_count grows, controller backs off and emits a diagnostic trace.

Related work: builds on ENG-2876 (tenant throttler refactor) and ENG-3011 (telemetry v2).

Checklist: 
- [x] Controller implementation + unit tests
- [x] Throttler integration (advisory hint handling)
- [x] Telemetry exports and dashboard skeleton
- [x] Canary rollout plan and feature flag
- [x] Docs (internal runbook)

Potential risks: over-aggressive integral accumulation during long sustained under-provisioning (mitigated by anti-windup and bounded integral), unintended interference with operator-initiated maintenance (mitigated by hard limit precedence), and metric skew due to cross-tenant aggregation (we added per-tenant bucketing).

Next steps after merge: schedule a 24h canary, monitor the new metrics, and collect two incident-free days before wider rollout. If we see hint_conflict_count spikes, revert via feature flag immediately.
